summary:
Yes. The tangent-edge obstruction does occur for the sets SCIP uses for implied minor equations, and the gaps are larger than in the bilinear case.

**What SCIP uses (read in the source, then tested).** Only sepa_interminor builds S-free sets for minors. It is off by default (freq = -1). Even when switched on, it returns at once unless SCIP is linked with Ipopt, although it never calls Ipopt. So the local binary (IPOPT=OFF) never separates minors; PySCIPOpt's bundled SCIP does when the separator is enabled.

**SCIP's set is the polar-decomposition set (proved).** The set is C_U = {M : sym(U^T M) ⪰ 0}, where M̄ = UP is the polar decomposition of the minor's LP value. This is exactly Bienstock–Chen–Muñoz's set (14a) with their λ of (17a). In a targeted run, all 258 cuts SCIP applied matched the C_U cut; the largest normalized difference was 4.5e-15.

**The orbit and its subfamilies (proved).**
- Under the automorphisms M ↦ AMB^T (and transposition), the orbit of SCIP's set is the 3-parameter family {C_F : det F > 0}. These sets are already maximal, so there is no completion step as in the bilinear case.
- The family contains a 2-parameter point-rule subfamily (F^T M̄ symmetric positive definite: SCIP's construction after every change of coordinates) and the 1-parameter BCM family (every λ). SCIP's set is the unique common member of the two.

**Structural results (proved).**
- A tangent edge forces any orbit set into a one-parameter pencil (homogeneous version of sfree Lemma 13).
- Corner minimizers have support at most 3, and support 3 needs s̄ to lie in the span of three rays. Every support-2 minimizer lies on a tangent edge.
- The sfree bilinear counterexamples embed as lower-dimensional minor corners.
- A fixed set such as SCIP's can attain z_K only if a corner minimizer lies in its 2-dimensional contact cone.
- SCIP's choice depends on variable scaling. Rescaling one problem variable turns a corner where SCIP's cut is optimal into one where it gives 2√δ·z_K. The point-rule and orbit families are scale-invariant and stay optimal.

**Exact counterexamples (certified in rational arithmetic).**

| Instance | Minimizer | Orbit | Point rule | BCM | SCIP |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | tangent edge | ≤ 9/20, bracket [0.4495347, 0.4495363] | ≈ 0.1976 | ≈ 0.3173 | 0.1358 |
| S1 | support one, all edges transversal | ≤ 0.779 | 0.4543 | 0.4855 | 0.312 |

- Instance A is a full-dimensional simplicial corner in R^4 with z_K = 1, attained only on the tangent edge. The gap persists on a neighbourhood of the data.
- Instance S1 also has z_K = 1, a unique minimizer at a vertex, and strictly positive multipliers on the other rays.
- SCIP values are computed in 50-digit arithmetic, not certified.

**Numbers (numerical).**
- *Random corners, 4 rays (600):* the orbit attains z_K in 593, the point-rule family in 521, BCM in 435, SCIP's set in 5 (mean ratio 0.883). All 12 random misses (N = 4 and N = 8) are certified exactly.
- *McCormick LP vertices of random bipartite bilinear programs (157):* the orbit attains z_K in all of them, SCIP's set in 12 (mean ratio 0.92–0.93).
- *Adversarial search:* with every invariant non-degeneracy margin at least 1%, the orbit ratio reached 0.200 (certified exactly for the rounded corner). That value is set by the margin; with a 5% margin the best was 0.326.

**Solver relevance (negative or weak).**
- Attaining z_K does not by itself give a better LP bound after re-solving. With the max-margin orbit set the bisection returns, the gap closed was lower than with SCIP's cut: 0.70 vs 0.78.
- The optimal orbit set nearest to SCIP's set did slightly better than SCIP's cut: 0.800 vs 0.778 and 0.777 vs 0.771 on the two sizes.
- These cuts are off by default in SCIP 10, so nothing here shows a benefit inside SCIP.

results.claim: sepa_interminor is the only SCIP 10.0.3 component that builds S-free sets for minors. It is off by default (freq -1) and returns immediately unless Ipopt is linked, although it never calls Ipopt. The local binary (IPOPT=OFF) makes 0 calls even with freq 0; PySCIPOpt's SCIP (Ipopt 3.14.19) calls it (1 call, 8 cuts found, 1 applied on the probe model). nlhdlr_quadratic Case 1 (also off by default) uses the same set for an explicit homogeneous constraint (from the source; not tested).

Proposition 1: SCIP's minor set (det M̄ > 0) is C_U = {M : sym(U^T M) ⪰ 0}, M̄ = UP polar decomposition; it equals BCM (14a) with lambda of (17a); for det < 0, the column swap gives {M : sym(W^T M) ⪰ 0} with W the orthogonal polar factor.

Fidelity: SCIP's applied interminor cuts equal the predicted C_U intersection cuts: 258 of 258 matched (60 random bipartite bilinear models), max normalized difference 4.5e-15; SCIP's literal step formula agrees with C_U to 1.4e-13 on 1709 rays.
results.location: note.md Section 2; code/scip_fidelity.py; logs/scip_fidelity_3x3.log, logs/scip_fidelity_4x4.log, logs/test_core.log

results.claim: Lemma 2 and Proposition 3: S-free sets of a minor are exactly the closed convex subsets of {det >= 0} with interior; maximal ones are cones (MPS C_Gamma, infinite-dimensional). The automorphism orbit of SCIP's set is {C_F : det F > 0} (3 parameters, all maximal). The point rule under all automorphisms gives PR = {C_F : F^T M̄ symmetric PD} (2 parameters, equivariant); the BCM family is {C_R : R in SO(2)}; BCM ∩ PR = {C_U}.
Proposition 4: the best one-cut bound of each family (orbit, PR, BCM) is found by bisection over 2x2 LMIs; rational positive definite dual certificates prove upper bounds exactly.

Proposition 5: for S = {det = 0}, minimizers with injective P_J have support <= 3; support 3 only if sbar lies in the span of three rays; every support-2 minimizer lies on a tangent edge with det(d) >= 0.
Lemma 6: a tangent edge at M0 = a0 b0^T forces F^T = theta(G0 + kappa G1), G0 = J adj(D), G1 = J adj(M0) (homogeneous version of sfree Lemma 13).

Corollary 7: sfree bilinear corners embed as minor corners with identical z_K and orbit bound, so sfree Theorem 14 (0.97539), the second instance (0.83477) and Proposition 16 (0.98385) are lower-dimensional minor counterexamples; reproduced numerically.

Theorem 8 (instance A): rational, full-dimensional simplicial corner in R^4 with z_K = 1, unique minimizer on a tangent edge. No orbit set contains T*, z_orbit <= 9/20 (exact bracket [0.4495347, 0.4495363]); point rule [0.1975640, 0.1975643]; BCM [0.3172917, 0.3172929]; SCIP 0.1358 (50-digit arithmetic). The gap persists on a neighbourhood of the data. Instance B: orbit [0.92194, 0.92196], SCIP 0.325.

Theorem 9 (instance S1): support-one minimizer, all edges transversal, strictly positive multipliers, z_K = 1, yet z_orbit <= 779/1000 (bracket [0.7780998, 0.7781193]); point rule 0.4543, BCM 0.4855, SCIP 0.3121.

Proposition 10: a fixed set C attains z_K only if every corner minimizer lies in C ∩ S; for C_F this is a 2-dimensional cone. With a unique support-one minimizer on ray j, SCIP's set attains z_K only if xhat(p_j) is parallel to xhat(sbar).

Proposition 11: SCIP's choice depends on variable scaling. On a corner obtained by rescaling one variable by delta, z_SCIP = 2 sqrt(delta) z_K, BCM < 11.1 sqrt(delta) z_K (numerically about 4 sqrt(delta)), while a point-rule set (hence the orbit) attains z_K; in the original scaling SCIP's set attains z_K.

Random corners (600 with 4 rays, 300 with 8 rays): supports 1 and 2 only. The orbit attains z_K in 593/600 and 295/300 (all 12 misses certified exactly, worst 0.775); point rule 521/274; BCM 435/240; SCIP 5/6 (mean ratio 0.883/0.936).
LP corners of random bipartite bilinear McCormick relaxations (86 at 3x3, 71 at 4x4): the orbit attains z_K in all; point rule 83/69; BCM 73/59; SCIP 5/7 (mean ratio 0.922/0.931).

LP re-solve: the bisection's max-margin orbit set closes less of the single-minor gap than SCIP's cut (0.702 vs 0.778; 0.706 vs 0.771); the optimal orbit set nearest to SCIP's set closes slightly more (0.800 vs 0.778; 0.777 vs 0.771). A better corner bound alone does not improve the LP bound; no evidence of a solver-level benefit.

Adversarial search with invariant non-degeneracy margins of 1%: orbit ratio down to 0.200; all 10 final corners certified exactly after rounding (smallest exact bound 0.20033). With 5% margins, 0.326. The minimum is set by the margin; heuristic upper bound on the worst case.
Principal minors with det(M̄) > 0: the PSD (or NSD) cone is the unique maximal S-free set, so SCIP's set attains the best single-cut bound z_K there.

corrections_to_earlier_notes: No errors found in the earlier notes. One precision for sfree section 10.2: the sets C_F are not merely 'related to' BCM's outer-product-free minor sets. BCM's (14a) sets are exactly the rotation members C_R of the orbit, and SCIP's minor set is the member C_U, where U is the polar factor. The question sfree section 10.2 left open, whether the tangent-edge obstruction also occurs for the minor sets, is answered yes.
open_questions: Is there a quantitative non-degeneracy condition on the optimal simplex under which the orbit attains z_K for minors? Instance S1 shows that transversality alone is not enough.
Is the worst-case orbit ratio bounded away from 0 under invariant non-degeneracy margins? The search reached 0.200 at 1% margins and 0.326 at 5%.
Which tie-break among the sets attaining z_K gives good LP bounds after re-solving, and does any beat SCIP's point-rule set over several rounds inside SCIP?
Is the closure of the orbit family's cuts exact for minors?
For minors with a diagonal entry (S' = {det = 0, a >= 0}), which maximal S'-free family attains the corresponding corner bound?
solver_relevance: Low. In SCIP 10.0.3, minor intersection cuts are off by default, and the local Ipopt-free build can never run them. When they are enabled (PySCIPOpt's bundled SCIP), the set used is C_U, confirmed cut by cut. That set is not scale-invariant and almost never attains the corner bound, whereas the orbit (and largely the point-rule) family does. But after re-solving the LP, the bound-optimal set gains more than SCIP's cut only if it is chosen close to SCIP's set (+0.006 to +0.022 of the gap on average); the max-margin choice gains less. No experiment inside SCIP's cutting loop or on MINLPLib/QPLIB was run.
